problem: Long-lived agent branches must not start a commit from a product-main state that was already stale, while concurrent product-main commits created after the agent HEAD must not retroactively invalidate that push.
authority: Git commit ancestry between origin/private/neko-overlay-v1 and the pushed agent/** HEAD

selected.mechanism: existing private-overlay GitHub Actions workflow + git fetch + merge-base --is-ancestor
selected.behavior: For agent/** pushes, resolve the newest product-main first-parent commit whose committer timestamp is at or before the agent HEAD committer timestamp; require that commit to be an ancestor. A newer product-main commit created after the agent HEAD is reported as PASS_RACE and becomes mandatory on the next agent push.
selected.reason: Uses the repository's existing CI and Git's native ancestry semantics; adds no scheduler, branch database, bot or second governance service.

considered.reason: already executes on every agent/** push
native exact ancestry check; no custom branch graph logic
current connector lacks Administration write access and branch protection primarily governs merge, not all long-lived direct agent pushes
duplicates repository CI governance for a deterministic Git graph check

acceptance: Every ordinary agent/** push fetches current product main.
The newest product-main commit available at or before the agent HEAD commit boundary must be an ancestor of the agent HEAD.
Product-main commits created after the agent HEAD do not retroactively fail that already-created agent commit.
If current product main advanced after the agent HEAD, the run reports PASS_RACE and the next agent push must resync.
Reuse/architecture/plugin/release gates remain unchanged and execute after freshness.
race_safety: prevents moving-target false failures during concurrent product-main and agent development while still blocking a genuinely stale next implementation commit
